fieldNotes.site: Ultium Cells - Spring Hill TN, the GM / LG Energy Solution JV 2.8M sq ft battery-cell plant built on land leased from GM at the Spring Hill Manufacturing campus, 100 Saturn Pkwy, Spring Hill (Maury County) TN. The roster/address geocode pin (the red marker in probe imagery) lands at the SW corner of the bright white-roof plant building. The Ultium complex is the NE corner of the broader GM campus, ~1.2 km NE of the main Cadillac assembly plant cluster. Center locked at 35.7490,-86.9525.
fieldNotes.confirm: Confirmed by satellite + Street View + web research. The complex is two connected large industrial buildings: a bright white-roof main battery plant (E, ~35.749,-86.951, brand-new clean construction) and an adjoining gray-roof logistics/warehouse building (W, ~35.749,-86.956). 2026-02/03 Street View shows the operational white plant building, employee lots full of cars, chain-link perimeter fencing along the access road, and campus checkpoint signage. The DOE Environmental Assessment for the Spring Hill battery plant explicitly lists 'shipping and receiving areas... a guard house, hazardous materials storage' as attendant structures.
fieldNotes.truckGate: True. Chain-link perimeter fence is clearly visible along the public approach road in 2026-03 Street View; the truck approach runs from a controlled campus road network (STOP sign, bollard delineators, blue directional/checkpoint signage) into the fenced plant. A battery plant of this security/IP/hazmat profile inside a secured GM campus operates a controlled truck gate.
fieldNotes.guardShack: True (medium confidence). The DOE EA for this plant lists a 'guard house' among attendant structures, and a small booth-footprint structure sits beside the entrance road at the campus checkpoint (~35.7480,-86.9508). The exact booth could not be resolved crisply in overhead imagery, hence medium. remoteGs false as a consequence.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Banded 25-50 (est. ~28). A dock apron with trailers backed in runs along the inner/north face in the gap between the two buildings (multiple red/white trailers visible at z19), plus a dock bank facing the north trailer yard. Roof angle and the building-to-building gap obscure an exact count; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: True (medium). Two distinct building faces serve trucks: the main white plant's dock face (cell shipping / finished goods) and the gray logistics building's dock face on the west, implying physically separate ship/receive clusters. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Banded 10-25. A dedicated paved trailer drop yard sits north of the building gap (~35.7510,-86.9540) with ~15-22 trailers parked in angled and straight rows in the captured imagery. dropYard true.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: ~60 est. across the north drop yard and dock apron staging; approximate.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: True - the access road and laydown/staging apron south of the gate provide truck-sized waiting room before the fenced entrance.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: True - paved internal yard between the gate and the dock banks holds queued trucks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: True - the gate-to-dock internal approach is long (several hundred meters of campus road), easily holding a 3+ truck queue.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: True (medium) - the campus entrance has wide paved/graded width and a multi-lane road network with room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Est. 2 in / 2 out at the entrance road (medium confidence).
fieldNotes.railServed: True - an active rail line runs along the NW edge of the complex (visible diagonally in z18 imagery just past the trailer drop yard), serving the GM Spring Hill campus.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: True - the Ultium complex is two large connected buildings (white battery plant + gray logistics/warehouse) plus utility structures; and it sits within the larger multi-building GM campus.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural - Spring Hill / Maury County is a small-town / edge-of-town setting; the campus is greenfield with surrounding farmland.
fieldNotes.imagery: Some surrounding ground in the Maxar/Airbus tiles still shows construction-era grading and laydown, but the plant buildings, dock apron, trailer drop yard, employee lots and fencing are all clearly built out and operational. Counts are honest overhead estimates.
fieldNotes.geofence: perimeter ring (~110 acres) traces the fenced Ultium complex core: both buildings, the north trailer drop yard, the dock aprons and the south employee lots, oriented to the slightly-rotated building grid. truckGate quad aligns to the entrance drive at the SE; dropYards covers the north trailer lot; dockAprons covers the inter-building dock strip and the gray building's west dock face.

citations.claim: GM PR states the Spring Hill TN plant is operated by Ultium Cells LLC, the GM / LG Energy Solution joint venture, not by GM directly.
Spring Hill is an Ultium Cells JV plant (GM/LGES); cells are pivoting to LFP energy-storage supplied to LG Energy Solution Vertech.

verification.rationale: JV the account does not operate: Spring Hill is run by Ultium Cells LLC (GM/LG Energy Solution joint operating company), not GM. Protocol excludes JVs the account does not operate. Built on GM-leased land but operated by the JV. (No bankruptcy-era / RACER divestiture issue here; plant is new construction.)
